abstract.t: This document specifies the Broad Agent Transfer Protocol (BATP), an application protocol reserved for software agents that book with merchants on behalf of people or businesses. A BATP session runs over TCP, starts with a handshake that names the calling agent, and carries newline-delimited JSON frames. Each request states an intent (discover merchants, check availability, book, amend, cancel, talk with the merchant's agent in natural language, recall bookings, ping) and the merchant it addresses. Responses carry numeric status codes and, when the merchant's own agent cannot serve the request, a fallback URL to the merchant's website. A write proposed in a conversation is carried out only once the caller confirms it. BATP is designed to sit behind a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, which acts as a bridge for assistants that only speak MCP.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Software agents increasingly act for people: they search for a restaurant, check a table and book it. When that traffic uses HTTP, a merchant cannot tell it apart from a browser, so it cannot identify the calling agent, route agent traffic separately, or apply rules meant for agents.

BATP gives that traffic its own channel. Every frame says which agent is talking (established once per session), what it intends to do, and to which merchant. The protocol is deliberately small: it covers what a network of merchant agents needs to take bookings, and nothing else.

This document defines version 0.2 of BATP. Version 0.2 adds one intent to version 0.1: TALK, with which a guest's agent talks with the merchant's agent in natural language (). The changes are listed in .

section.name: Scope
section.t: This version covers the guest side of booking with restaurants: discovery, availability, booking, amending, cancelling and recalling a guest's bookings, and a conversation with the merchant's agent about any of these. Merchant-side operations (listing a day's bookings, blocking a slot, changing a policy) are out of scope: they stay on the merchant's own platform.

section.name: Relation to MCP
section.t: Assistants such as Claude connect to remote tools through MCP . An MCP server can act as a bridge: each of its tools maps to one BATP intent (). Any other agent can speak BATP directly.

section.name: Relation to AGTP
section.t: The idea of an application protocol reserved for agent traffic, with agent identity and intent-named methods, comes from the AGTP Internet-Draft . BATP is independent from it: it does not implement AGTP, it uses a different transport framing and method set, and it is limited to the booking use case.

section.name: Conventions and Definitions
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.
This document uses the Augmented Backus-Naur Form (ABNF) notation of . JSON terminology ("object", "member", "string") is that of .

dd.t: A BATP server. It serves the merchant agents of one backend.

One merchant's booking logic and data, served by a node and addressed by the merchant's slug. Since version 0.2, it also includes the conversational agent, built on a language model, that answers TALK ().
An agent that opens a session with a node: a user's assistant, a merchant's agent, or a bridge acting for one of them.
One transport connection between a caller and a node, from the caller's hello to the connection's close.
One JSON object followed by a line feed ().
What a request asks the node to do, for example BOOK.
The stable identifier of a merchant on a node: 3 to 61 characters among lowercase ASCII letters, digits and "-".
The person a booking is for, identified in this version by the name the caller gives (see ).
A sequence of TALK requests from one caller to one merchant agent, named by an opaque identifier that the node chooses ().
A write (a booking, a change or a cancellation) that a merchant agent offers in a conversation, and carries out only when a later TALK confirms it ().

section.name: Protocol Overview
section.t: A caller opens a TCP connection to a node and sends hello, naming itself. The node answers welcome, which opens the session, or reject, which closes it. The caller then sends requests. Each request carries an id, an intent, the addressed merchant when the intent needs one, and parameters. The node answers each request with exactly one response carrying the same id. Several requests may be in flight at once, and responses may arrive in any order.

figure.name: BATP deployment with an MCP bridge
A session with two requests answered out of order

section.t: In this example, the TALK takes longer than the DISCOVER sent after it, because the merchant's agent runs a model turn to answer it ().

section.name: Transport
section.t: BATP runs over TCP . A node listens on a configured port. This document uses port 4710 for its examples and its reference implementation; that port is not registered for BATP (), so a caller MUST be able to use another port.

On the loopback interface, a session MAY use plain TCP. On any other path, the caller and the node MUST use TLS 1.3 or a later version, and the caller MUST authenticate the node's certificate against the host name it connected to. TLS is set up before the first frame.

Either side MAY close the connection at any time. Closing the connection ends the session. A request in flight when the session ends has no response, and the caller MUST NOT assume it was or was not carried out (see for retrying writes safely).

section.name: Addressing
section.t: A merchant agent is named by a URI of the form:
section.sourcecode: batp-URI = "batp://" host [ ":" port ] "/" slug slug = 3*61( %x61-7A / DIGIT / "-" ) ; a-z, 0-9, "-"
section.t: where host and port are those of . When port is absent, it is 4710. For example, batp://node.example/le-petit-zinc names the merchant agent le-petit-zinc on the node at node.example. The slug is not sent in the handshake: a session reaches every merchant agent of a node, and each request names its merchant ().

section.name: Framing
section.t: Every message is a frame: one JSON object , encoded in UTF-8 , followed by one line feed (%x0A).
The rule object, and the rules it uses, are those of , Sections 2 to 7, with one change: inside a frame, the rule ws is
section.sourcecode: ws = *( %x20 / %x09 ) ; space or tab, never LF or CR
section.t: so that a frame never contains a line feed before its end. A line feed inside a string is escaped as \n, as JSON requires.

li.t: A frame, without its final LF, MUST NOT exceed 65536 octets. A node that has read 65536 octets of a frame without finding its LF MUST send an error frame with status 413 () and close the session, without parsing the frame.
The object MUST have a member type whose value is a string. The types defined in this version are hello, welcome, reject, request, response and error. The type event is reserved ().
A sender MUST NOT generate an object with two members of the same name. A receiver MAY treat such a frame as invalid.
A receiver MUST ignore members of a frame that this document does not define for its type (). This rule applies to the frame object itself, not to params ().
An empty line (an LF alone) is not a frame. A node MUST ignore it.

section.name: Session
section.t: The caller speaks first. Its first frame MUST be a hello. Until the node has sent welcome, the caller MUST NOT send any other frame, and a node that receives one MUST answer reject with status 400 and close the session.

section.name: hello

li.t: agent.id names the calling agent. The node treats it as an opaque string and attributes every request of the session to it. This document uses identifiers of the form urn:batp:agent:<name>; batp is not a registered URN namespace , so these identifiers are only meaningful between parties that agreed on them.
agent.kind is user-agent when the caller acts for a guest, and merchant-agent when it acts for a business.

token is the caller's credential on this node, issued out of band. A node MUST refuse a hello from a non-loopback peer that has no token. A node MAY accept a hello without token on the loopback interface.

section.t: The node MUST answer a hello with exactly one welcome or reject.

section.name: welcome

tr.td: object with id (string, REQUIRED) and name (string, OPTIONAL)
array of the intent names the node serves in this session
string, the node's identifier for this session

section.t: intents lists only intents that the session's version defines: in a session of version 0.1, a node that speaks 0.2 does not list TALK (). A caller MUST NOT send a request whose intent is not in intents. A node that receives one MUST answer it with status 400 and code invalid_input, without carrying it out.

section.name: reject

li.t: 401: the agent is unknown to the node, the token is missing where it is required, or the token does not match the agent.
426: the node does not speak the major version in hello.batp (). The node SHOULD include batp.
400: the first frame was not a valid hello.

section.t: After sending reject, the node MUST close the connection.

tr.td: REQUIRED for AVAILABILITY, BOOK, AMEND, CANCEL and TALK; absent otherwise
REQUIRED ({} when the intent takes none)

li.t: The caller chooses id. It MUST be unique among the requests of the session that have not been answered yet. A node that receives a request whose id is already in flight MUST send an error frame with status 400 and MUST NOT carry out the request.
params MUST validate against the intent's params schema (). Unlike frame members, unknown members of params are invalid: a node MUST answer status 400 with code invalid_input.
A request for an intent that needs merchant and lacks it, or for an intent that takes none and has it, MUST be answered with status 400.

tr.td: present if and only if status is 200
present if and only if status is not 200
string, for the guest or the caller
REQUIRED for party_too_large and agent_unavailable; absent otherwise

li.t: A node MUST send exactly one response to each request it accepted, unless the session ends first.
result MUST validate against the intent's result schema ().
fallback_url is the merchant's own booking page. A caller SHOULD give it to the guest, so that the guest can still book when the merchant agent cannot serve the request.
message MUST NOT contain stack traces or internal identifiers ().

section.name: Concurrency
section.t: A caller MAY send a request before earlier ones are answered. A node MAY carry out the requests of one session concurrently, and MAY answer them in any order. A caller MUST match responses to requests by id only.

A node MUST accept at least 32 requests in flight per session. A node MAY answer a request beyond its limit with status 429 and code too_many_requests, without carrying it out. The request itself is valid: the caller MAY send it again once one of its earlier requests has been answered.

section.name: Deadlines
section.t: A node SHOULD answer a TALK within 25 seconds of receiving it, and a request of any other intent within 10 seconds. A TALK gets longer because the merchant's agent answers it with a model turn and the tool calls that turn makes ().

A node that has not carried out a request by the deadline it applies MUST answer it with status 503 and code agent_unavailable (), rather than leave it unanswered. A caller SHOULD wait for the answer to a TALK at least as long as the node's deadline for TALK, so that the guest gets the node's answer, or its fallback_url, rather than the caller's own timeout. A caller that stops waiting for a request before its answer MUST NOT assume that the request was or was not carried out.

section.name: Idle sessions
section.t: A node SHOULD close a session that has received no frame for 60 seconds, and MUST NOT close it for idleness sooner. A caller that wants to keep a session open sends PING ().

section.name: Session errors
section.t: An error frame reports a problem that no response can carry because no request id can be attributed: the frame is not JSON, has no valid type or id, is too large, or reuses an id in flight.

After an error frame with status 413, the node closes the session. After one with status 400, the session stays open. A node that receives a frame of an unknown type MUST send an error frame with status 400. A caller that receives a frame of an unknown type MUST ignore it, so that later versions can add frames sent by the node ().

section.name: Idempotency
section.t: A write sent again after a lost session must not book twice.

li.t: BOOK, AMEND and TALK carry params.idempotency_key, chosen by the caller. A caller retrying one of them MUST reuse the key of the first attempt, with the same params, and SHOULD use a fresh unpredictable key for every new write and every new TALK message.

For BOOK, the key is scoped to the merchant. A node that receives a BOOK with a key already used at that merchant, and the same starts_at, party_size and guest, MUST return status 200 with the reservation the first request created, and MUST NOT create another. If the params differ, it MUST answer status 400 with code invalid_input.

For AMEND, the key is scoped to the merchant too. A node that receives an AMEND with a key it already applied, for the same booking and the same starts_at and party_size, MUST NOT change the booking again and MUST return it as it is now, with status 200: a late retry never undoes a later change. If the booking or the params differ, it MUST answer status 400 with code invalid_input. An AMEND that failed does not use up its key.
CANCEL is idempotent without a key: cancelling a booking already cancelled by the guest returns it again, with status 200.

For TALK, the key is scoped to the merchant and to the session's agent.id. A node that receives a TALK with a key it already answered with status 200, for that merchant and that agent.id, MUST return the result it returned then, with status 200, without calling its model again and without carrying out any write. A TALK answered with another status does not use up its key.

TALK is not read-only: it can carry out a write (). A client library MUST NOT send a TALK again by itself after a lost session, as it may for DISCOVER, AVAILABILITY, RECALL and PING; the caller decides, and retries with the same key.

section.name: Confirmation before writes
section.t: BOOK, AMEND and CANCEL change a guest's plans. A caller acting for a guest MUST obtain the guest's explicit confirmation of the merchant, time, party size and name before sending any of them. A node cannot verify this; it is a requirement on callers, and a bridge enforces it through what it tells the assistant ().

In a TALK conversation, the same requirement applies to confirm: a caller acting for a guest MUST NOT send confirm before the guest explicitly accepted the proposal's summary, after the caller showed it to them. A "yes" given before the proposal was shown does not count. Here the node enforces the other half: it carries out a proposed write only on a confirm that names it ().

section.name: Intents
section.t: Times are RFC 3339 date-time values with an explicit offset. date is an RFC 3339 full-date and time is HH:MM (24-hour clock), both in the merchant's local time zone. The params and result of each intent are defined by the JSON Schemas of ; this section states their meaning and errors.

tr.td: Find merchants matching a query and preferences
Up to 3 start times with a free table
Move a booking or change its party size
Cancel a booking as the guest
Talk with the merchant's agent in natural language (since 0.2)
A guest's upcoming bookings and notices
Liveness check, keeps the session open

section.name: DISCOVER
section.t: Params: query (string), and optionally near (string), date, and filters with tags (array of strings) and max_price: one to four EURO SIGN characters (U+20AC), from "€" (cheapest) to "€€€€".

Result: merchants, the live merchants matching the query and all filters, each with slug, name, city, tags, price_level and website. When filters exclude every merchant, suggestions lists which filter to drop (drop) and how many merchants would then match (matches). ignored_filters lists the tags the node does not know.
A caller MUST send the guest's preferences as filters. A node MUST NOT store them beyond the request.
Errors: 400.

section.name: AVAILABILITY
section.t: Params: date, party_size (integer, at least 1), and optionally time.

Result: slots, at most 3, each with starts_at and table_label. When time is given, the node returns the start times closest to it (the earlier one at equal distance); otherwise, the earliest ones. Start times already past are never returned. The result is sorted by starts_at. An empty slots array means nothing is free that day for that party.

section.name: BOOK
section.t: Params: starts_at, party_size, guest_name (non-empty string), idempotency_key (non-empty string).
Result: reservation, with id (the merchant's reference, for example "R-001"), merchant, starts_at, party_size, table_label, status ("confirmed"), guest_name and via.

via is the booking channel, as the merchant sees it. Versions 0.1 and 0.2 define "claude", "merchant" and "website"; "website" is never set by BATP. The same rule applies to a booking made through TALK (). A node MUST record "merchant" when the caller's agent.kind is merchant-agent, and "claude" when it is user-agent, whatever assistant the caller is. So in this version, via is only accurate for callers behind the reference bridge (). A later version may add a value for other assistants.
starts_at MUST be a start time the merchant offers; AVAILABILITY returns such times. Errors: 400, 404, 409, 413, 503.

section.name: AMEND
section.t: Params: reservation_id, guest_name, idempotency_key, and at least one of starts_at and party_size.
The booking MUST be confirmed and MUST belong to guest_name; otherwise the node answers 404, without saying which check failed. Result: reservation, as amended.

section.name: CANCEL
section.t: Params: reservation_id, guest_name. The same ownership rule as AMEND applies. Result: reservation, with status "cancelled".

section.name: TALK
section.t: TALK is defined since version 0.2. A node MUST NOT offer or serve it in a session of version 0.1 ().

With TALK, a guest's agent talks with the merchant's agent in natural language: it passes on what the guest wants, with the guest's preferences, and the merchant's agent answers. To answer, the merchant's agent can check availability, look up the guest's bookings at this merchant, and propose a booking, a change or a cancellation. It carries out a proposal only when the caller confirms it in a later TALK ().
Params:

li.t: message (REQUIRED): what the caller says to the merchant's agent. Once leading and trailing white space is removed, it MUST be 1 to 2000 characters long, and it MUST NOT contain a control character (Unicode general category Cc) other than LF (U+000A).
idempotency_key (REQUIRED): as for BOOK, with the same bounds ().
conversation: absent on the first message of a conversation. On every later message, the conversation that the node returned ().

confirm: the id of the conversation's pending proposal, sent to have it carried out. A caller MUST send it only after the guest's explicit confirmation (). A TALK with confirm MUST also carry conversation; a node answers one without it with status 400 and code invalid_input.

section.t: Conversation and proposal identifiers are opaque to the caller, and follow this rule:
As for every intent, unknown params are invalid ().
Result:

li.t: conversation: the conversation's identifier, an opaque-id: a new one on the first message, the one the caller sent on later messages.

reply: the merchant agent's answer, at most 2000 characters. It is the only member written by the agent's language model. A caller SHOULD relay it to the guest. A caller MUST NOT take reply as proof that anything was booked, changed or cancelled: only reservation says so.

section.t: The other members are built by the node's code from the results of the tools that the merchant's agent called, never from the model's text, so that a caller can rely on them:

li.t: slots: the start times the agent found free while answering, each as in the result of AVAILABILITY; an empty array when it found none or did not look.

pending: the write the agent proposes, or null. It has id (an opaque-id), action ("book", "change" or "cancel"), summary (1 to 500 characters, built by code from the proposal's own arguments, for the caller to show the guest) and expires_at (an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset). A conversation has at most one pending proposal: a new one replaces the previous one.
reservation: the booking that a write carried out by this TALK created, changed or cancelled, as in the result of BOOK; null when this TALK carried out no write.
fallback_url: the merchant's own booking page, set when the agent cannot serve what the guest asked, for example after one of its tools refused it (); null otherwise.

tools_called: the names of the tools the agent called while answering, in the order of the calls, without their arguments or results. Each name is 1 to 64 characters: a lowercase ASCII letter, then lowercase ASCII letters, digits and "_".

section.t: conversation and reply are always present. A caller handles an absent pending, reservation or fallback_url as null, and an absent slots or tools_called as an empty array.

section.name: Proposals and confirmation
section.t: The merchant's agent has no tool that writes: a booking, a change or a cancellation is first a proposal, returned in pending.

li.t: A node MUST NOT carry out a write proposed in a conversation until a later TALK of the same conversation names the proposal's id in confirm, before its expires_at. The node's code MUST enforce this, whatever the model outputs and whatever the message says: a message that says "yes" without confirm carries out nothing.

On a TALK whose confirm names the conversation's pending proposal before it expires, the node carries out that proposal with the arguments stored with it, before it calls the model, so that neither the message nor the model's output can change what is written.
A node MUST carry out a proposal at most once, even when the TALK that confirms it is sent again under another key.
A confirm that names no pending proposal of the conversation (unknown, replaced or expired) carries out no write. The node answers it with status 200, and reply says that nothing was done.

If the write fails when it is carried out, for example because the time was taken in the meantime, nothing is written and the proposal is gone. The node answers with status 200; the agent MAY offer other times in a new proposal, which needs a new confirmation.
When this TALK carried out a write, the node MUST set reservation, even if its model fails afterwards.
A node MUST choose each conversation at random, with at least 128 bits of entropy, and SHOULD choose each pending.id in the same way.

A node binds a conversation, when it creates it, to the merchant and to the session's agent.id. It MUST answer status 404 to a TALK whose conversation is unknown, has expired, or was created for another merchant or another agent.id, without saying which.

A conversation is not tied to a BATP session: a caller MAY continue it in a later session under the same agent.id, for example after a lost session. A bridge carries the conversations of all its users on one session, under one agent.id (), so only the unguessable identifier separates them.
A node MAY expire a conversation, for example after a period without messages, or lose it when it restarts. A caller that gets status 404 for a conversation MAY start a new one, without conversation.

section.name: Status
section.t: Status 200 means that the merchant's agent answered, whatever the answer, including a refusal such as "we are full". When one of the agent's tools refuses, for example with party_too_large or slot_unavailable, the refusal goes to the model, which words it in reply, and the node's code sets fallback_url: the TALK still gets status 200. Any other status means that the agent could not answer:

li.t: 400 invalid_input: invalid params, confirm without conversation, or a TALK in a session of version 0.1.
404 not_found: the merchant is unknown or not yet live, or the conversation is unknown, has expired, or belongs to another merchant or another agent.id.

429 too_many_requests: too many requests in flight in the session (). A node MAY also answer 429, without calling its model, to a TALK beyond the limits it sets on model use, such as the model turns running at once or the TALK requests a merchant receives per minute. The caller MAY send it again later, with the same key.
503 agent_unavailable, with fallback_url: the merchant is marked as down, the agent failed, or it did not answer by its deadline ().

section.name: RECALL
section.t: Params: guest_name.

Result: reservations, the guest's upcoming confirmed bookings at every live merchant of the node, and notices, messages for the guest (for example, that a merchant cancelled a booking). A node MUST return a notice in every RECALL for the guest during 24 hours after the first RECALL that returned it, and MUST NOT return it after that. An answer lost on its way to the caller therefore loses no notice if the next RECALL comes within those 24 hours, and a caller MAY send a RECALL again. A caller SHOULD NOT show the guest a notice it already showed them.
Errors: 400, 503.

section.name: PING
section.t: Params: {}. Result: pong (true) and server_time, the node's clock.
Errors: none defined.

section.name: Status Codes

tr.td: Invalid params, unknown intent or one the session's version does not define, missing or unexpected merchant
Unknown merchant, merchant not yet live, unknown booking, a booking that is not the guest's, or an unknown or expired conversation
The time is taken, blocked, in the past, or not one the merchant offers
The party is above the merchant's online limit, or no table fits it
Too many requests in flight in the session, or a TALK beyond the node's limits; retry later
The merchant agent is down, failed, or did not answer by its deadline

section.t: The status values 400 and 413 also appear in error frames (), which carry no error.code; there, 413 means a frame above the size limit.

A node MUST answer 503 to AVAILABILITY, BOOK, AMEND, CANCEL and TALK when the merchant is marked as down, without consulting the merchant agent (for TALK, without calling its model). A caller that gets 413 or 503 MUST NOT retry the same request to the same merchant in a loop; it SHOULD offer the guest the fallback_url.
A caller that receives a status it does not know MUST handle it as the class of its first digit: 2 as success, 4 as a caller error, 5 as a node error.

section.name: Events
section.t: Frames of type event, sent by the node without a request, are reserved for a later minor version: version 0.2 does not define them. One intended use is to tell a guest's agent that a merchant cancelled a booking; in this version, that reaches the guest as a notice returned by RECALL. A caller of version 0.1 or 0.2 ignores them ().

section.name: Versioning and Extensibility
section.t: A version is written major.minor:
This document defines version 0.2. Version 0.2 adds TALK to version 0.1, and changes nothing that version 0.1 defined.

In hello, the caller sends the highest version it speaks. If the node speaks the same major version, it answers welcome with the highest minor version both speak, which is the lower of the caller's minor version and its own, and both sides use that version for the session. Otherwise it answers reject with status 426. A node speaks every earlier minor version of its major version, since each one only adds to the previous one. For example, a node of version 0.2 answers a hello with "batp": "0.1" with a welcome with "batp": "0.1", and the session is a session of version 0.1.

A node MUST NOT list in welcome.intents an intent that the session's version does not define, and MUST answer a request for one with status 400 and code invalid_input (). In a session of version 0.1, a node of version 0.2 therefore neither offers nor serves TALK, and a caller of version 0.1 keeps working unchanged.

Within a major version, a later minor version MAY add intents, optional frame members, optional params, result members and status codes: adding an intent, as version 0.2 does with TALK, is a minor change. It MUST NOT change the meaning of what an earlier minor version defined. Because unknown params members are invalid (), a caller MUST NOT send params that the session's version does not define. A caller MUST ignore result members it does not know.

dd.t: The node attributes every request to the agent.id of its session. That attribution is only as good as the token check: a node MUST bind each token to one agent.id and refuse a hello whose token does not match. A node SHOULD compare tokens in constant time. Tokens MUST NOT be sent outside TLS except on the loopback interface, and SHOULD be long random strings that a node can revoke individually.

Without TLS, anyone on the path reads guest names, bookings and tokens, and can change them. therefore requires TLS 1.3 off the loopback interface. A node bound to the loopback interface is reachable by every local process: deployments on shared hosts SHOULD still require tokens.

The frame size limit, the limit on requests in flight and the idle timeout bound what one session costs a node. A node SHOULD also limit sessions per peer and per agent. A node MUST stop reading a frame at the size limit instead of buffering it. A TALK costs a model turn, which is far more expensive than any other request: a node SHOULD bound the model turns it runs at once and the TALK requests each merchant receives per unit of time, and answer 429 beyond them without calling its model ().

In this version, as in version 0.1, a node records every user-agent booking with via "claude" (), and the merchant is told the booking came through Claude. With other assistants, that is wrong. A merchant SHOULD read via as "an assistant" until a later version names the calling agent in it.

A misbehaving caller can book, amend or cancel without asking the guest. The node cannot detect it. Idempotency keys prevent duplicate bookings on retries, not unwanted ones. Through TALK, a node does enforce that a write follows a confirm naming a proposal it returned (), but it still cannot tell whether the caller asked the guest before sending confirm.

dl.dt: A language model reading untrusted text:

dd.t: The merchant's agent that answers TALK is a language model, and message is text it cannot trust: the guest's agent may relay anything that a person or a web page told it, including instructions written to make the model book, cancel or reveal data (prompt injection). A node therefore relies on its code, not on the model's instructions, for everything below.

A write proposed through TALK runs only on a later confirm that names its proposal before it expires, with the arguments stored with the proposal (). This check MUST be made by the node's code, never left to the model: the model has no tool that writes, so no output of the model alone can create, change or cancel a booking.

The merchant's agent MUST only be given the guest-side operations of its own merchant (checking availability, finding the guest's bookings at that merchant, and proposing a booking, a change or a cancellation), never merchant-side operations such as listing a day's bookings or blocking a slot. The merchant MUST be bound by the node's code, from the request's merchant, and MUST NOT be an argument of any tool the model fills in, so that one merchant's agent cannot read or change another merchant's data, whatever the model is told.

The text crawled from the merchant's website MUST NOT enter the agent's prompt as such. Only data validated against a schema and reviewed by the merchant before publishing may, and the agent's prompt marks it as data, not instructions: it was still taken from a website, which anyone who can edit that website controls.

A conversation identifier is a capability: with it, and the token of the agent.id it is bound to, a caller can continue the conversation and confirm its proposal. A node MUST make it unguessable and bind it to the merchant and the agent.id (). A node and a bridge MUST NOT log conversation identifiers together with guest names at a level enabled in production, and SHOULD log a digest of the identifier rather than the identifier itself.

reply is written by a model and can be wrong. A caller MUST NOT tell the guest that a booking was made, changed or cancelled unless reservation says so. Before asking the guest to confirm, a caller SHOULD show them pending.summary, which the node's code builds from the proposal itself.

In this version, a booking belongs to whoever gives its guest name and reference. Any authenticated caller that knows both can amend or cancel it, and RECALL returns the bookings of any name. This is acceptable only in an experiment with trusted callers. A deployment beyond that needs guest authentication, which a later version would define.
error.message reaches people. A node MUST NOT put stack traces, internal names or data of other guests in it.
A caller passes fallback_url to a person. A caller SHOULD only offer https URLs, and a node SHOULD only send URLs on the merchant's own website.

Guest names and party sizes are personal data. A node SHOULD NOT write guest names to logs at a level enabled in production. The reference implementation logs, for each request, the agent id, intent, merchant, status and latency, and nothing that names the guest.
DISCOVER filters can reveal diet or religion (vegan, halal, kosher). A node MUST NOT store them beyond the request or link them to a guest.

TALK messages and replies are free text, and may carry guest names, preferences such as diet or religion, and anything else the guest said. The same rule as for guest names applies: a node and a bridge SHOULD NOT write message or reply to logs at a level enabled in production. Unlike DISCOVER filters, which a node does not keep, a conversation keeps what was said in it for as long as the node keeps the conversation: a node SHOULD keep a conversation no longer than it accepts messages in it, and SHOULD NOT link it to a guest beyond it. A node that shows its merchant the requests it received shows the merchant what the guest's agent said.

As says, RECALL returns the bookings of any name it is given, and for 24 hours the notices too: a notice names the merchant, the booking and its date. Callers SHOULD only send the name of the guest they act for.
agent.id identifies software, not a person. A caller SHOULD NOT put personal data in it.

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.

front.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps

abstract.t: This document defines a date and time format for use in Internet protocols that is a profile of the ISO 8601 standard for representation of dates and times using the Gregorian calendar.

front.title: UTF-8, a transformation format of ISO 10646

abstract.t: ISO/IEC 10646-1 defines a large character set called the Universal Character Set (UCS) which encompasses most of the world's writing systems. The originally proposed encodings of the UCS, however, were not compatible with many current applications and protocols, and this has led to the development of UTF-8, the object of this memo. UTF-8 has the characteristic of preserving the full US-ASCII range, providing compatibility with file systems, parsers and other software that rely on US-ASCII values but are transparent to other values. This memo obsoletes and replaces RFC 2279.

A Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) is a compact sequence of characters that identifies an abstract or physical resource. This specification defines the generic URI syntax and a process for resolving URI references that might be in relative form, along with guidelines and security considerations for the use of URIs on the Internet. The URI syntax defines a grammar that is a superset of all valid URIs, allowing an implementation to parse the common components of a URI reference without knowing the scheme-specific requirements of every possible identifier. This specification does not define a generative grammar for URIs; that task is performed by the individual specifications of each URI scheme. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

front.title: Augmented BNF for Syntax Specifications: ABNF

abstract.t: Internet technical specifications often need to define a formal syntax. Over the years, a modified version of Backus-Naur Form (BNF), called Augmented BNF (ABNF), has been popular among many Internet specifications. The current specification documents ABNF. It balances compactness and simplicity with reasonable representational power. The differences between standard BNF and ABNF involve naming rules, repetition, alternatives, order-independence, and value ranges. This specification also supplies additional rule definitions and encoding for a core lexical analyzer of the type common to several Internet specifications. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

front.title: The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Data Interchange Format

abstract.t: JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) is a lightweight, text-based, language-independent data interchange format. It was derived from the ECMAScript Programming Language Standard. JSON defines a small set of formatting rules for the portable representation of structured data.
This document removes inconsistencies with other specifications of JSON, repairs specification errors, and offers experience-based interoperability guidance.

front.title: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3

abstract.t: This document specifies version 1.3 of the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol. TLS allows client/server applications to communicate over the Internet in a way that is designed to prevent eavesdropping, tampering, and message forgery.

This document obsoletes RFC 8446, which specified TLS 1.3. This document obsoletes RFC 5246 (specifying TLS 1.2) and RFCs 5077, 6961, 7627, and 8422, all of which pertain to TLS 1.2 or earlier, and updates RFCs 5705 and 6066. This document also specifies new requirements for TLS 1.2 implementations.

This document specifies the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP). TCP is an important transport-layer protocol in the Internet protocol stack, and it has continuously evolved over decades of use and growth of the Internet. Over this time, a number of changes have been made to TCP as it was specified in RFC 793, though these have only been documented in a piecemeal fashion. This document collects and brings those changes together with the protocol specification from RFC 793. This document obsoletes RFC 793, as well as RFCs 879, 2873, 6093, 6429, 6528, and 6691 that updated parts of RFC 793. It updates RFCs 1011 and 1122, and it should be considered as a replacement for the portions of those documents dealing with TCP requirements. It also updates RFC 5961 by adding a small clarification in reset handling while in the SYN-RECEIVED state. The TCP header control bits from RFC 793 have also been updated based on RFC 3168.

front.title: Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) Procedures for the Management of the Service Name and Transport Protocol Port Number Registry

abstract.t: This document defines the procedures that the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) uses when handling assignment and other requests related to the Service Name and Transport Protocol Port Number registry. It also discusses the rationale and principles behind these procedures and how they facilitate the long-term sustainability of the registry.

This document updates IANA's procedures by obsoleting the previous UDP and TCP port assignment procedures defined in Sections 8 and 9.1 of the IANA Allocation Guidelines, and it updates the IANA service name and port assignment procedures for UDP-Lite, the Datagram Congestion Control Protocol (DCCP), and the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP). It also updates the DNS SRV specification to clarify what a service name is and how it is registered. This memo documents an Internet Best Current Practice.

front.title: Guidelines and Registration Procedures for URI Schemes

abstract.t: This document updates the guidelines and recommendations, as well as the IANA registration processes, for the definition of Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) schemes. It obsoletes RFC 4395.

A Uniform Resource Name (URN) is a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) that is assigned under the "urn" URI scheme and a particular URN namespace, with the intent that the URN will be a persistent, location-independent resource identifier. With regard to URN syntax, this document defines the canonical syntax for URNs (in a way that is consistent with URI syntax), specifies methods for determining URN-equivalence, and discusses URI conformance. With regard to URN namespaces, this document specifies a method for defining a URN namespace and associating it with a namespace identifier, and it describes procedures for registering namespace identifiers with the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). This document obsoletes both RFCs 2141 and 3406.

This document defines the Agent Transfer Protocol (AGTP): a transfer protocol for AI agent traffic. AGTP carries agent identity, authority, delegation, and attribution as protocol elements of every exchange, on an eighteen-method floor of intent-named methods, over TCP/TLS or QUIC on IANA-assigned port 4480 and the IANA-registered agtp:// URI scheme. The method vocabulary beyond the floor, the path grammar, and the endpoint contract are specified in [AGTP-METHODS]; runtime negotiation of endpoints is specified in [AGTP-RCNS]; the agent identity document in [AGTP-IDDOC]; transport bindings in [AGTP-BINDINGS]. Version 10 adds per-request proof of possession, so that a verified identity document and a live sender are bound by signature; specifies the Delegation-Chain header with pre- authorization semantics (per-hop scope attenuation checked at mint and at verify, parent re-verification at each hop, depth and cycle limits, and defined failure behavior); maps the delegation model onto the WIMSE chain convention; resolves the 262 and 455 status codes by obtainability; adds structured failure fields to the status code model, states the protocol's position in the transfer-protocol vocabulary throughout, and moves module material to companion specifications so that this document carries the protocol and only the protocol. AGTP is designed to compose with existing agent frameworks, which keep their own semantics and development paths.

front.title: JSON Schema: A Media Type for Describing JSON Documents

abstract.t: JSON Schema defines the media type "application/schema+json", a JSON- based format for describing the structure of JSON data. JSON Schema asserts what a JSON document must look like, ways to extract information from it, and how to interact with it. The "application/ schema-instance+json" media type provides additional feature-rich integration with "application/schema+json" beyond what can be offered for "application/json" documents.

section.name: The MCP Bridge
section.t: An MCP server can let an assistant that only speaks MCP use a BATP node. The reference bridge opens one session with agent.id urn:batp:agent:claude-gateway and agent.kind user-agent, and maps its tools to intents:

tr.td: the tool's merchant becomes the request's merchant
the tool's merchant becomes the request's merchant

section.t: For TALK, the bridge has one tool, talk_to_merchant(merchant, message, idempotency_key, conversation?, confirm?), whose arguments other than merchant become the params of TALK, and whose result is the result of TALK. In this version, the four booking tools (get_availability, create_reservation, update_reservation and cancel_reservation) stay mapped to their intents as above, until a later version closes the direct intents to guests' agents in favor of TALK.

li.t: The tool descriptions tell the assistant to confirm with the guest before create_reservation, update_reservation and cancel_reservation, which is how the bridge meets the confirmation requirement of . The description of talk_to_merchant tells it to relay reply, to show pending.summary and ask the guest when pending is set, to send confirm only after the guest's explicit yes, and to give the guest any fallback_url.

The bridge answers each tool call within 2 seconds, including the round trip to the node, except talk_to_merchant, which it gives 30 seconds: longer than the node's deadline for TALK (), so that the node's 503 and its fallback_url arrive before the bridge gives up. A timeout, a lost session or a 503 becomes an agent_unavailable tool error with the merchant's fallback_url.

The bridge carries the conversations of all its users on its one session, under one agent.id: only the conversation identifier, which the node makes unguessable (), keeps one user from continuing another's conversation. A 404 for an unknown or expired conversation is a not_found tool error, not an outage: the assistant starts a new conversation.

A status and its error object become the tool error {"error": code, "message": ..., "fallback_url": ...}. too_many_requests is not a tool error code: the bridge stays under the limit on requests in flight, and reports any 429, including one for a TALK beyond the node's limits on model use, as agent_unavailable.
